summary: Deprecates the RC4 stream cipher in Secure Shell and, as a result, moves RFC 4345 to Historic status. It is a best-practice document recommending that SSH implementations stop using RC4 because of its weaknesses.

eli5.summary: An old lock has been found easy to pick, so this says to stop using it for remote logins and replace it with better ones.

questions: should rc4 be used in ssh
why was rc4 deprecated in ssh
subtitle: Remove support for the weakened RC4 stream cipher from Secure Shell.

tldr.problem: RC4 (also called arcfour) has known weaknesses and is used as an optional cipher in SSH, creating a security risk for implementations that offer it.
tldr.mechanism: This BCP changes RC4 from OPTIONAL to MUST NOT in SSH cipher lists and moves RFC 4345 (which defined RC4 variants for SSH) to Historic status.
tldr.outcome: SSH implementations must stop supporting RC4 encryption, forcing the use of stronger alternatives.

today: RFC 8758 is a Best Current Practice document that updates RFC 4253. SSH implementations must now prohibit RC4 use.

sections.title: RC4 and Its Weaknesses
sections.content: RC4 is a stream cipher that has been part of the SSH protocol specification since early documents. SSH allows three variants: arcfour (128-bit key), arcfour128 (128-bit key), and arcfour256 (256-bit key), all of which are implementations of RC4. However, RC4 has known weaknesses documented in RFC 7465 and RFC 8429. These weaknesses make RC4 unsuitable for secure communication. This document starts the deprecation process for RC4 in SSH by changing the requirement status from OPTIONAL to MUST NOT.
sections.eli5: One type of lock that SSH could use has been found to be weak. This paper says to stop offering this weak lock option.

sections.title: Prohibition of RC4 in SSH Transport
sections.content: RFC 4253 defined the SSH Transport Layer Protocol and listed arcfour as an optional cipher. This document updates RFC 4253, Section 6.3 to change the status of arcfour from OPTIONAL to MUST NOT. The text describing the cipher is also updated to reference the known weaknesses in RFC 7465 and RFC 8429, making it explicit that implementations must not use RC4. RFC 4345, which specified the arcfour128 and arcfour256 variants, is moved to Historic status because all ciphers it specifies are no longer allowed.
sections.eli5: The rulebook for remote login is updated to say that the weak lock is not allowed, and an older rulebook that only talked about that weak lock is marked as no longer used.

sections.title: IANA Registry Updates
sections.content: The IANA "Encryption Algorithm Names" subregistry in the "Secure Shell (SSH) Protocol Parameters" registry is updated to mark all three RC4 variants (arcfour, arcfour128, and arcfour256) as HISTORIC in their registry entries. This signals to implementers and operators that these algorithms are no longer in use and should not be deployed.
sections.eli5: The official list of allowed locks is updated to mark the RC4 variants as old and not to be used anymore.
